candidate_boot_identity.note: Both segments come from one reset-backed boot captured at 09:23:06; segment 2 is a continuation with no reset.

scenario: Saved credentials absent from scan results — the boot the hidden-SSID gap used to break

operator_confirmation.who_configured_the_network: Nobody in this session. The device booted on the credentials already in NVS; the AP appeared on its own.

timeline_ms.event: No AP on saved channels, starting full scan
SAVED_DIRECT_FALLBACK candidates=2  <- the new fallback engages
No more AP to connect, next scan in 10 seconds  <- bounded backoff, queue exhausted

observed_properties.fallback_trigger_scope: Only after a successful all-channel scan found no saved network: the saved-channel scan ran first, escalated to a full scan, and the fallback only then produced candidates.
observed_properties.candidate_cap_and_dedup: candidates=2, matching the two distinct valid saved credentials; the cap of three was not reached.
observed_properties.one_connect_call_per_candidate: Each candidate produced exactly one 'WiFi connecting to <ssid>' line, then a disconnect and advance — no five-fold repeat of the same fallback entry.
observed_properties.bounded_backoff: After the queue drained the station armed 'next scan in 10 seconds' and did retry at 27163, 10s later.
observed_properties.retry_succeeded: The second fallback cycle associated and obtained a DHCP lease.
observed_properties.no_driver_config_or_start_failures: No CONNECT_CONFIG_FAILED or CONNECT_START_FAILED, and no SCAN_COMPLETION_FAILED, appeared in either segment.
observed_properties.stability_after_association: From 36.3s to the end of segment 2 no disconnect, no config mode and no connect timeout occurred; NETWORK_EVENT stayed at 2.

hidden_ssid_evidence.device_side: The device associated with SSID JianGuanJu, which the all-channel scan did not list as a match, via the direct path that uses channel 0 and no pinned BSSID.
hidden_ssid_evidence.host_side: An independent host WLAN survey taken in the same period lists 7 visible SSIDs — one of them an empty/hidden name plus DIRECT-*, ChinaNet-*, HP-* and nova 13 — and JianGuanJu is not among them.
hidden_ssid_evidence.conclusion: A network that does not advertise its SSID was joined on boot. This is the exact gap the network stage set out to close, and on this boot it is closed.
not_claimed: I did not verify a wrong-password case.
I did not verify reconnect after the AP is switched off and back on.
A scan finding no match is not proof the AP was absent; the host survey is what makes hidden rather than absent the better explanation here.

network_rows.visible_ap_priority_preserved: PASS (no visible match existed this boot; the direct queue was used only after the full scan returned nothing)
network_rows.visible_ssid_boot_association_and_ip: NOT_VERIFIED (no visible saved AP was on the air)
network_rows.ap_off_then_on_reconnect: NOT_VERIFIED (needs the operator to toggle the AP)
network_rows.bounded_return_to_config_portal: PARTIAL (backoff observed and bounded; the portal was never reached because the device associated at 36.3s, before the board 60s deadline)

limitations: This is one boot on one network; it does not establish success rates.

The privacy-relevant SSID names appear in the private logs and are not reproduced in committed files; the SSID names quoted here are needed to describe what was verified and are already public in the earlier device reports.
No credentials, no audio and no NVS content are committed.
result: PASS on the fallback and hidden-SSID rows; four network rows remain NOT_VERIFIED/partial
